title: Detailed balance and phase transition in Nash equilibria of mean-field Ising game
authors: Ken Hiura, Hajime Koike, Kiyoshi Kanazawa
abstract: We study a finite-state mean-field game with entropic control cost. In the large population limit, we show that its stationary Nash equilibria satisfy the detailed balance condition and their distributions take the Gibbsian form with the value function playing the role of a Hamiltonian. We apply the entropic control cost to a ferromagnetic mean-field Ising game and investigate its stationary and non-stationary Nash equilibria. We find that the stationary Nash equilibria exhibit a second-order phase transition from disordered to ordered equilibria as temperature decreases. A center-manifold reduction yields non-stationary Nash equilibrium near the critical temperature and reveals the critical slowing down in the relaxation toward the stationary Nash equilibrium.
summary: This paper analyzes a mean-field Ising game incorporating an entropic control cost to study its equilibrium states. It demonstrates that the stationary Nash equilibria obey detailed balance and undergo a second-order phase transition characteristic of the mean-field Ising model. The work provides detailed critical dynamics, including critical slowing down, for both stationary and non-stationary regimes.
main_problem: The study investigates the detailed balance and phase transition behavior within the Nash equilibria of a mean-field Ising game incorporating an entropic control cost.
main_result: The stationary Nash equilibria satisfy detailed balance and exhibit a second-order phase transition from disordered to ordered states as temperature decreases. Critical dynamics are characterized by mean-field Ising scaling exponents.
method: The analysis uses the large population limit to derive a Mean-Field Game (MFG) system, followed by bifurcation analysis and center-manifold reduction to study non-stationary dynamics near criticality.
model_or_system: The model is a finite-state mean-field game based on the Ising model, where players minimize a cost function combining ferromagnetic interaction energy and an entropic control cost. The system is analyzed in the thermodynamic limit (large population N).
key_observables: Magnetization ($m$), difference in value function ($\Delta$), and relaxation time ($	au$).
important_parameters: Inverse temperature ($ eta$), critical inverse temperature ($ eta_c$), and interaction strength ($J$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the mean-field approximation ($N 	o \infty$) and the use of the instantaneous relative entropy rate as the control cost.

paper_structure: The paper first derives the MFG system in the large N limit, establishing the self-consistency equation for stationary states. It then performs a bifurcation analysis to locate the critical point $ eta_c$, followed by a detailed non-stationary analysis using center-manifold reduction to characterize critical slowing down.
why_interesting: The connection between game theory (Nash equilibria) and statistical physics concepts like detailed balance and phase transitions provides a powerful, non-standard framework for understanding emergent collective behavior in complex systems.
